findings.description: Re-verification of ledger [106] (single mint time budget vs TimeoutStartSec). Mechanics are correct: start_us is captured before sweep(), fits() refuses any request whose delay+req_max would overrun GX10_MINT_MAX_ELAPSED (600), the sweep is capped at budget/2, and the fail_slow hold-off (300) is clipped to the remaining budget, so worst-case ExecStartPre is bounded well under TimeoutStartSec=900. Tests pin it: test_whole_mint_run_is_bounded_below_the_start_timeout asserts max_elapsed + req_max < timeout and holdoff <= max_elapsed; test_no_request_starts_when_it_cannot_finish_inside_the_budget proves zero curl calls when REQ_MAX exceeds the budget; test_hold_off_is_clipped_to_the_remaining_budget covers the clip. One wording inaccuracy only: the ledger text says the tests 'drive the curl stub with slow responses'; they do not. The bound is pinned by static analysis of the script plus the REQ_MAX>budget trick, not by a slow-responding stub. The ledger entry should be reworded, no code change needed.

Re-verification of ledger [107] (dedicated gx10-runner-isolation.service). The runbook unit is a DefaultDependencies=no oneshot ordered Before=network-pre.target and systemd-user-sessions.service, loading only table inet gx10_runner_isolation via nft -f, so the stock nftables.service 'flush ruleset' can no longer wipe it. The user@<uid>.service.d drop-in uses Requires=/After= on the isolation unit, so the ghrunner manager cannot start without the rules. test_isolation_unit_is_an_early_boot_oneshot, test_runner_user_manager_requires_the_isolation_unit and test_nft_ruleset_is_ordered_persistent_and_dual_stack pin all three facts and the DNS-exemption-before-local-drop ordering. Correct and pinned. Operational consequence worth stating in the runbook (already implied by [107]): stopping or failing the isolation unit propagates to the whole ghrunner user manager and all runner instances, which is the intended fail-closed behaviour.

Re-verification of ledger [104]/[112] (unlabelled-job placement check). job_lane() returns None for a job with no labels, and verify_run treats None on any non-skipped job as a 'placement is unproven' violation rather than silently classifying it as hosted. test_job_that_ran_without_labels_is_a_placement_violation is parametrized over both lanes and both job kinds, so the check would fail if the None branch were removed. Correct and pinned.

The carve-out added to test_job_has_no_if_guard only checks that the fork-guard step's if: starts with the runner.environment prefix. A regression that keeps the prefix but drops the event-allowlist clause (for example `runner.environment == 'self-hosted' && true`) would still pass here and the step would still be exempted from the no-if-guard assertion. The fork guard itself is pinned in skills/tests/ci_runners/test_fork_guard.py, so this is defence in depth rather than a gap, but either assert the full canonical expression or delegate to the shared constant used by test_fork_guard so the two tests cannot drift apart.

Priority 3 check: nothing in this diff can plausibly cause the 12 full-suite failures in multiplayer-simulation and roadmap-runtime. git diff origin/main touches no file under skills/tests/multiplayer-simulation, skills/tests/roadmap-runtime, skills/roadmap-runtime, skills/multiplayer-simulation or skills/tests/conftest.py. The only shared-infrastructure change is appending tests/ci_runners to testpaths in skills/pyproject.toml. The new directory carries an __init__.py, so its modules import as ci_runners.test_* and cannot collide with the top-level module names of multiplayer-simulation (which has no __init__.py and relies on sys.path inserts in its conftest). The ci_runners conftest does not mutate sys.path or sys.modules. The report's own caveat that 'unrelated' is inferred from a control run rather than a main baseline is honest and sufficient; the remaining action is for the operator to confirm the same failures exist on main.

Priority 1 check: every on-branch claim in the report is backed by a named test or command (openspec validate --strict, 202 ci_runners tests, 862 workflow-parsing tests, the 477-test control run, the ruff TRY004 noqa, actionlint absent). O1 through O12 are listed under a skipped Pending-Operator Items section with evidence pointers and none is marked pass. No defect. One observability note for the operator rather than a finding against the branch: the Security phase is 'not applicable' per the accepted vocabulary in ledger [114], yet the report's own framing is that self-hosted runners executing PR code are a host code-execution surface. The static security evidence that does exist on-branch (sudo-removal build proof in the Containerfile, podman cap-drop/no-new-privileges flags, nftables ordering tests, fork guard tests) is spread across Spec Compliance and Evidence. A one-line cross-reference from the Security section to those tests would make the report self-contained without changing its status.
